name: BOOT HILL

subjects.name: MOTT'S MARKER
LOOK_AT: A marker for Obadiah Mott, erected by public subscription in the fifth year. Well kept. Flowers, even.
The flowers are wax. The undertaker's lilies, on loan for the look of the thing.
It is the best-kept grave on the hill, for a man nobody here ever buried.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing under it.
Nothing under it, still.
Wind across the stone. It has a lot of town to cover and it starts here.

subjects.name: PIKE'S NEIGHBOR
LOOK_AT: A grave, open, waiting, with my name on the marker. Frame has spelled it wrong.
The spade is still in the spoil heap, waiting for a decision that has already been made.
Frame's spelling is on the marker in paint. The undertaker has left room to correct it, and will not.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing, yet.
A trickle of dirt into the bottom of it. Practice.
Nothing yet, for the second time. The yet is doing a great deal of work.

LOOK_AT: My plot, my headboard, HE TUNED. I visit. It is restful, in the way of problems that have been filed.
The grass has started over it. I am the first man in Consolation to watch his own grave come in.
Someone has left a tuning peg on the headboard, a piano's. I know whose piano. I'm not going to say.
LISTEN_TO: Wind in the oats. My grave is the only one here whose tenant can review the accommodations, and I give it high marks.
Nothing. Not from me, and I'd know.
The oats again, and somewhere down the hill, a piano, in tune.

subjects.name: THE NINETEEN
LOOK_AT: AMOS TREADWELL. BLACKSMITH. 1850.
JOSIAH PENHALLOW. MINER, OF CORNWALL. 1851.
ELIAS CRANE. SURVEYOR. 1850.
RAFAEL SANDOVAL. MULETEER. 1852.
SILAS MARCHBANK. CLERK. 1851.
PATRICK KEANE. CARPENTER. 1853.
ABEL STROUD. GAMBLER. 1854.
ISAAC PELL. WHEELWRIGHT. 1855.
OWEN PROTHERO. COLLIER, OF GLAMORGAN. 1857.
The row ends. Nine names, nine trades, nine dates, and the same grass over all of them.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.
Nothing.

subjects.name: PIKE'S MARKER
LOOK_AT: Ezra Pike. The man I was sent to find. Six years.
A plain board, kept upright. The undertaker's work, and paid for, I would guess, by the undertaker.
I have his letter of introduction in my coat. It introduces me to this.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. I have come a very long way to hear it.
Nothing, still. He was never going to answer, and I keep asking anyway.
Wind in the grass over him, and that is all the reply there is.

overrides.TALK_TO: I read him my letter of introduction. It seemed only right. He took it as well as anything else I've said here.
overrides.USE: It's in use. That's the entire and only thing a plot can be.

subjects.name: THE FENCE
LOOK_AT: A rail fence down one side of the hill, as far as the gate. The other sides are left to good manners.
Split rails, pegged rather than nailed, and every peg tight. Somebody walks this fence.
It runs from the gate to the edge of the hill and stops, as if it had made its point.
LISTEN_TO: Wind in the rails, a low hum with no tune in it. I've looked for one.
A rail ticking as the night cools it. It's the only thing up here keeping time.
Nothing. Up here even the fence is careful how loud it is.

overrides.PUSH: It holds. The undertaker maintains it. His clients do not leave, but their reputation for it must be kept up.

subjects.name: THE HEARSE
LOOK_AT: My coffin is inside, behind the glass. The curtains are drawn, out of respect for a man who isn't there.
Black lacquer, brass lamps and a plume on the roof. I have never traveled in such style, and I am not traveling now.
The back door is on a latch. It is the kind of latch that assumes nobody inside will want out.
LISTEN_TO: The coffin shifts an inch every time the wind leans on the hearse. It weighs nothing, and she knows it.
A brass lamp ticking as it cools.
Nothing from inside. That is the whole problem.

overrides.PUSH: The deceased does not push. It would look keen.
overrides.PULL: It is attached to the mule, and the mule is attached to the ground.
overrides.PICK_UP: With what is in it, I very nearly could.

subjects.name: GRIEVANCE, AT THE GATE
LOOK_AT: Grievance, in black harness, standing at the gate as if it were a wall. Her head is turned toward the hearse.
She has carried every coffin in Consolation up this hill. She has never once been fooled, and she does not mean to start with mine.
Her ears are flat. The livery man would call it professional.
LISTEN_TO: A long breath out through the nose, aimed at the coffin.
Her harness creaks as she shifts her weight. She shifts it away from the hill.
Nothing. She has said what she has to say.

overrides.PULL: She considers the request, declines it, and goes on looking at the coffin.
overrides.PUSH: From behind? At a funeral? I would be the second thing they buried.
overrides.PICK_UP: She is in harness, and in no mood.

subjects.name: THE MOURNERS
LOOK_AT: Half the town, in black, at the gate. Nobody here has buried me before, and they would like to get it right.
They are standing the way people stand at a stopped coach, politely, looking at their watches.
Not one of them has looked at me twice. A low hat does more than I would have guessed.
LISTEN_TO: Somebody says I was a quiet sort of fellow. Somebody else says I was new. They agree that will be it.
A watch being wound, and then a second watch, out of sympathy.
Somebody asks whether the mule always does this. The undertaker says she has never done it before. Everybody looks at the coffin.

overrides.PICK_UP: They have come to carry me. It would confuse things to carry them.

subjects.name: THE UNDERTAKER
LOOK_AT: The undertaker, at Grievance's head in his good apron. He is the only man here who knows the coffin is empty, and he is sweating for both of us.
He keeps not looking at me, which is very nearly the same thing as looking at me.
He has a hand on her bridle. She allows it, the way she allows weather.
LISTEN_TO: He is murmuring to the mule. It sounds like an apology.
His boots shift on the gravel. He would like to be anywhere else, the box included.
Nothing. He has stopped murmuring. It was not working.

overrides.PICK_UP: He is holding the mule. Somebody has to.

subjects.name: REVEREND SOWERBY, AT THE GATE
LOOK_AT: Reverend Sowerby, with his book open at the place, ready to see me off.
There is a pencil behind his ear, for the counting.
He has not looked at me once. The clergy see the soul, and I am wearing a hat.
LISTEN_TO: He is turning pages to find his place, and finding it twice.
He hums the opening of a hymn under his breath, to see if it still fits.
Nothing. He is saving it.

THE GATE.CLOSE: It swings back. The latch is broken in the direction of welcome, which is not the direction you want a graveyard broken in.
